claims.text: The proposed coating consists of CrCoNi-based FCC high-entropy-alloy layers in a nanoscale multilayer architecture.
The layers are initially single-phase FCC.
Well-developed SRO is established during deposition.
Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading is governed by the evolution and eventual breakdown of SRO within individual multilayer layers.
Pre-deformation annealing can selectively alter and control the SRO level within each layer.
The comparison will expose the proposed mechanism by testing annealed and untreated multilayers under otherwise identical loading conditions.
Local degradation of SRO creates localized soft or rejuvenated zones.
Pre-annealing modifies the initial SRO state.
Breakdown of SRO reduces local energy barriers for dislocation nucleation and motion.
SRO degradation promotes a transition from reversible to irreversible stacking-fault behavior.
SRO-degraded regions act as nucleation sites for irreversible stacking faults and twin boundaries.
Formation of irreversible stacking faults and twin boundaries drives progressive plastic deformation.
Annealed samples with altered SRO will exhibit earlier localized plastic deformation than the as-deposited baseline.
In situ 4D-STEM will show a transition from reversible to irreversible stacking faults and twin boundaries under cyclic stress.
Deformation will become spatially concentrated in localized zones associated with degraded SRO.
The as-deposited baseline with preserved SRO will deform more homogeneously and at a later time.
The mechanism applies under sustained loading at room and moderately elevated temperatures.
Conditions dominated by grain-boundary diffusion or phase transformation fall outside the proposed mechanism.
A lack of statistically significant earlier onset or stronger localization in annealed samples, or a lack of correlation between SRO breakdown and deformation, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main test is described as sustained loading, but the predicted microscopy signature is specified under cyclic stress. The cited evidence also concerns cyclic loading, so the loading protocol for testing sustained-load deformation is internally inconsistent.
